metadata.methods_description: MEG recordings were acquired using a whole-head Elekta Neuromag Vector View 306 system (102 triple-sensor elements) in a magnetically shielded chamber at 1 kHz sampling rate with 0.03-330 Hz filtering. Eight task runs (~10 min each) were recorded along with a 2-minute resting-state recording (eyes open). Head position was tracked before each run using indicator coils. Electrode positions and fiducial points were digitized using a 3D Polhemus digitizer. High-resolution structural MRI was acquired on a Siemens 3T Magnetom Prisma Fit scanner (1 mm slice thickness, TR=2300 ms, TE=2.98 ms, flip angle=9°). Data were formatted in BIDS and anonymized using MNE-Python 1.8.0 and MNE-BIDS 1.6.0.

citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises raw magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 23 healthy adult participants performing an n-item delayed temporal reproduction task, designed to investigate the neural dynamics of working memory load indexed by alpha power. Participants maintained sequences of auditory intervals in memory and reproduced them via motor responses across eight task runs, with concurrent electro-oculogram and electrocardiogram recordings. The dataset includes structural MRI acquired on a separate day for source reconstruction and resting-state MEG, providing a resource for studying neural mechanisms of working memory and auditory-motor integration in the healthy adult brain.

citation_details.title: An updated herpetofaunal species inventory of Iona National Park in southwestern Angola
citation_details.author: Javier Lobón‐Rovira, Pedro Vaz Pinto, François S. Becker, Krystal A. Tolley, John Measey, Bruce Bennet, Bastiaan Boon, Sango de Sá, Werner Conradie
citation_details.abstract: Angola has experienced an incredible increase of the knowledge of its herpetofauna over the past decade. However, accurate biodiversity inventories remain deficient for certain regions of particular conservation interest. We therefore provide an updated checklist of Iona National Park&rsquo;s herpetofauna, with 75 recorded species, including five amphibians and 70 reptiles, 40 of these recorded for the first time in Iona National Park. These species comprise ~80% of the reptile diversity of Namibe Province. Therefore, this work recognises Iona National Park as the most reptile-diverse protected area in Angola and is potentially one of the richest in southern Africa. Consequently, this work enhances the importance of specific conservation plans in the area and the need for further investigation into the hidden biodiversity of this region.
